subject.title: fix(codex): reject hex/exponent computer wait duration strings

question: Should Codex computer timeout budgeting retain only plain decimal integer strings as compatibility input while preserving fractional JSON numbers, or must it also preserve fractional string durations accepted by another execution path?
rationale: Upstream Codex transports nested arguments as free-form JSON and public OpenClaw docs specify seconds but not a string grammar, so source inspection establishes the malformed-input risk without conclusively establishing which shipped string forms owners intend to preserve.

options.title: Confirm and align the grammar
options.body: Verify the computer tool schema and execution parser, then keep this patch if they accept numeric durations only or adjust both paths to the same canonical string subset.

options.title: Accept the narrowing
options.body: Merge the proposed decimal-integer-string compatibility rule and treat other string forms as unsupported malformed input.

options.title: Preserve fractional strings
options.body: Use a strict decimal parser that rejects hexadecimal and exponent syntax but continues accepting non-negative fractional decimal strings.

recommendation.title: Confirm and align the grammar
recommendation.body: Verify the computer tool schema and execution parser, then keep this patch if they accept numeric durations only or adjust both paths to the same canonical string subset.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal is recent ownership of the Codex app-server runtime and its timeout/configuration behavior.
